content: The Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research, established in 1982, is a non-profit organization dedicated to research and education. It is located in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The institute was founded as a financially independent entity separate from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). However, its members and associate members hold faculty appointments within MIT's Department of Biology. The Whitehead Institute is recognized as one of the world's leading centers for genomic research. Its Center for Genome Research played a significant role in the Human Genome Project, contributing approximately one-third of the human genome sequence that was announced in June 2000. In June 2003, Eli and Edythe L. Broad pledged $100 million to establish the Broad Institute, a collaborative initiative involving the Whitehead Institute, MIT, Harvard University, and local teaching hospitals. The mission of this new venture is to develop advanced tools for genomic medicine and apply them to the treatment of various diseases. The Whitehead Institute boasts a globally renowned faculty. Among its members is Robert Weinberg, the recipient of the 1997 National Medal of Science. Additionally, the faculty includes eight members of the National Academy of Sciences: Gerald Fink, Rudolf Jaenisch, Eric Lander, Susan Lindquist, Harvey Lodish, Terry Orr-Weaver, David Page, and Robert Weinberg. Three of its members—Fink, Lander, and Weinberg—are also members of the Institute of Medicine. Furthermore, six faculty members—Jaenisch, Fink, Lander, Lindquist, Lodish, and Weinberg—are fellows of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. All Whitehead faculty members are also affiliated with MIT's Department of Biology. Members of the institute hold tenured positions as full or associate professors, while associate members are on tenure-track appointments. The institute also maintains an Affiliate Members program.
